newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares set new record, rise seen continuing.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares set new record, rise seen continuing.

text.p: Danish share prices stormed to a new record high on Friday, buoyed by the strong dollar and keen foreign buying interest, and dealers saw the advance continuing next week.
"I think that the KFX will rise by half a percent on Monday if there is good demand for the A.P.Moeller companies, which is likely given the dollar's position just now," a dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index closed at 155.67, 1.19 up from Thursday's close -- itself a record.
The KFX March future rose 1.55 point to 155.30, with 335 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Overall bourse turnover was 1.6 billion crowns.
International shipping group A.P. Moeller's D/S Svendborg rose 4,000 crowns to 280,000 but its D/S 1912 was unchanged at 193,000.
Danisco rose four crowns, to 370, but the dealer said that the company was ripe for a sharp rise, having completed repayment of a 1.15 billion crown bond on Friday.

"In the very near future we see Danisco reaching 400 crowns," he said, adding that he believed that ISS remained undervalued, despite rising 10 crowns to 189. --Morten Pedersen, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
